proof:
Source: step 5 of the parent proof (the competitor Z₁ = T + (push Y)|_U: (i) same boundary, (ii)–(iii) compact support of Z₁ − T in A ∩ B_{G₃}, (iv) B_{G₃} ⊂⊂ U, and minimality), with the cycle push Y replaced by an arbitrary X and B_{G₃} by W. Simon 7.1.1 and 7.2.4 with Remark 7.2.5(2). Siblings: (IMC) im_calculus, part (c); (RO) restrict_open_im.
Notation. For D ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^P), D|_U := D.restrictDomain(U ⊆ ℝ^P) ∈ 𝒟_k(U), so D|_U(ω) = D(ω) for ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U), regarded in 𝒟^k(ℝ^P) with the same underlying form. For a current D in a domain V, spt D = V ∖ Z_D, where Z_D is the union of the open sets W′ with compact closure contained in V on which D vanishes; Z_D is open. Currents are determined by their values (GeometricCurrentOn.ext).
1. (Z₁ is integer multiplicity.) T is integer multiplicity (first part of IsMinimizingIn T A). X|_U is integer multiplicity by (RO), U being open. By (IMC)(c) in U, N := X|_U − X|_U, then N − X|_U, then T − (N − X|_U) are integer multiplicity. For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U): (T − (N − X|_U))(ω) = T(ω) − (0 − X(ω)) = T(ω) + X(ω) = Z₁(ω). Hence Z₁ = T − (N − X|_U) is integer multiplicity.
2. (∂Z₁ = ∂T.) Let η ∈ 𝒟^m(U). The form dη ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), regarded in 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P), is the exterior derivative of η regarded in 𝒟^m(ℝ^P): both have underlying form dη (exteriorDerivativeTestOn does not depend on the domain). Hence ∂Z₁(η) = Z₁(dη) = T(dη) + X(dη) = ∂T(η) + ∂X(η) = ∂T(η), because ∂X = 0. So ∂Z₁ = ∂T, which is SameBoundary Z₁ T in degree n = m + 1.
3. (spt(Z₁ − T) ⊆ spt X.) For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), (Z₁ − T)(ω) = Z₁(ω) − T(ω) = X(ω). Let x ∈ spt(Z₁ − T); then x ∈ U. Suppose x ∉ spt X. Then x ∈ Z_X: there is an open V ∋ x on which X vanishes. As U is open, choose r > 0 with B_r(x) ⊆ U and put V′ := V ∩ B_{r/2}(x). V′ is open and contains x; closure(V′) ⊆ closedBall(x, r/2) ⊆ B_r(x) ⊆ U, and closure(V′) is compact (a closed subset of the compact closedBall(x, r/2)). For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ V′ ⊆ V: (Z₁ − T)(ω) = X(ω) = 0. So Z₁ − T vanishes on V′ and x ∈ Z_{Z₁−T}, contradicting x ∈ spt(Z₁ − T). Hence spt(Z₁ − T) ⊆ spt X ⊆ A ∩ W.
4. (Compactness.) spt X ⊆ W ⊆ closure(W) ⊆ U. Therefore spt(Z₁ − T) = U ∖ Z_{Z₁−T} equals spt X ∩ (ℝ^P ∖ Z_{Z₁−T}): '⊆' by step 3, and '⊇' because every point of spt X lies in U. This is the intersection of the compact set spt X with a closed set, hence compact.
5. (Minimality.) W is open with W ⊂⊂ U, Z₁ is integer multiplicity (step 1), SameBoundary Z₁ T (step 2), and spt(Z₁ − T) is compact (step 4) and contained in A ∩ W (step 3). The second part of IsMinimizingIn T A, applied to W and S := Z₁, gives M_W(T) ≤ M_W(Z₁). ∎
key_steps: Z₁ = T − ((X|_U − X|_U) − X|_U) is integer multiplicity by (RO) and (IMC)(c).
∂Z₁(η) = T(dη) + X(dη) = ∂T(η) because ∂X = 0; so SameBoundary Z₁ T.
(Z₁ − T)(ω) = X(ω); a point of U outside spt X has a small open neighbourhood with compact closure in U on which Z₁ − T vanishes, so spt(Z₁ − T) ⊆ spt X ⊆ A ∩ W.
spt(Z₁ − T) = spt X ∖ Z_{Z₁−T} is compact; minimality with W and S = Z₁ gives M_W(T) ≤ M_W(Z₁).
